Marissa / team —

We can support an interim attestation / bridge letter. High-level plan and caveats:

Option A — Bridge letter (fastest):
- We provide a signed bridge/interim attestation that references our most recent SOC 2 Type II report (report date 2026-12-31), enumerates control families in scope (CC1–CC7), and confirms there have been no material control changes affecting the control objectives through 2027-05-05.
- Required customer-facing artifacts for legal: control-change log since 2026-12-31, summary of security incidents (redacted), latest vulnerability scan summary, and vendor patch cadence documentation.
- Internal gating: Security must validate the control-change log and incident summary; target turn time = 48–72 hours if info is available and legal signs off on redaction levels.

Option B — Evidence addendum (longer):
- Produce an addendum package with sampled evidence supporting the control families. This can take 7–10 business days depending on sample assembly and auditor involvement.

Next steps I can own: provide a bridge-letter draft (template attached) and a checklist of evidence items needed from internal owners and legal. If Sales confirms they want Option A, we will open a 72-hour sprint with Security, Compliance, and Legal.

Jonas, can you confirm we have the most recent vulnerability scan and the control-change log accessible? Karthik, can Legal prep signatory language for the bridge letter?

- Rishi
